0.content:
Abyss Order (also: Order of the Abyss, the Abyss Order): The Abyss Order is a secretive legion of intelligent monsters of the Abyss, such as Abyss Mages, Heralds and Lectors, who hate the Seven and Celestia and work to overthrow the world the gods rule. Most of its members were once people of Khaenri'ah, the godless nation destroyed 500 years ago, who were cursed into monstrous forms. It was founded by Chlothar Alberich after the cataclysm and is now led by the Traveler's lost twin, whom the Order reveres as its Prince or Princess. Dainsleif hunts it constantly.

Leadership: The Traveler's twin sibling (Lumine if the player chose Aether, Aether if the player chose Lumine) leads the Order. Their goal is to restore Khaenri'ah and confront the Heavenly Principles, and they refuse to reunite with the Traveler until their war against the gods is over.

Goals: The Order wants revenge on the gods for destroying Khaenri'ah, an end to the curse on its people, and the rebirth of Khaenri'ah.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Order is active. It holds the Atlas of New Khaenri'ah and needs only a place to set it down. Its leader was last seen in Snezhnaya with Asmoday.

1.content:
Adventurers' Guild (also: Adventurer's Guild, Adventurers Guild): The Adventurers' Guild is Teyvat's adventurer-for-hire service. It gathers word-of-mouth information and requests from ordinary people and organisations and redistributes them as commissions for registered adventurers. Its motto is "Ad astra abyssosque" (to the stars and the abyss), though in practice the work runs from finding lost kittens to exploring domains. Every region has a branch or post with a receptionist named Katheryne; most known branches are led by a Branch Master. Its headquarters is in Snezhnograd, Snezhnaya.

Structure: One branch (or reception post) per region; most known branches are run by a Branch Master (none is named for Inazuma or Fontaine). Katheryne receives adventurers at each. Known branch masters: Cyrus (Mondstadt), Lan (Liyue), Kamal (Sumeru), Mansa (Natlan), Sarin (Nod-Krai).

Status as of 7.1: Active everywhere. As of 7.1 it still operates posts in all eight regions, with Katheryne at each.

2.content:
Alberich Clan (also: Alberich, House Alberich, Alberich family): The Alberich Clan is an old, pure-blooded noble family of Khaenri'ah, the sunken kingdom destroyed in the cataclysm 500 years ago. It was known for producing leaders of the kingdom's knights. It is not royal, but members stepped in as regents when King Irmin failed. Its present-day line includes Kaeya, the Cavalry Captain of the Knights of Favonius, who was raised in Mondstadt as Kaeya Alberich.

Members: Anfortas, the Knight Marshal and regent; Chlothar, founder of the Abyss Order; Kaeya, the present-day Cavalry Captain of the Knights of Favonius.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Alberich Clan exists only in the shadows. Its only publicly known member is Kaeya, who lives in Mondstadt and does not serve the clan's agenda.

key: School of the Theory of Living Things
3.content:
Amurta (also: Amurta Darshan, School of Biology, School of the Theory of Living Things, Darshan of Biology): Amurta is the Sumeru Akademiya's school of biology, which also covers ecology, botany and medicine. It is recognised as the oldest and largest of the Six Darshans, and its colour is green. Its sage is Naphis, a famously short-tempered man of integrity who is now also the Akademiya's Grand Sage. Tighnari, the Forest Watcher, graduated from Amurta under Naphis.

Leadership: Naphis is Amurta's Sage. Tighnari calls him a man of integrity who sticks to his beliefs. Researchers fear his legendary temper, and even the former Grand Sage Azar gave him leeway.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Amurta is led by Naphis, who is also Grand Sage. No Amurta-specific story was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

4.content:
Arataki Gang (also: Arataki-ha, Arataki's Gang, the Arataki Gang, Itto's gang): The Arataki Gang is a small band of friends in Hanamizaka, a district of Inazuma City, led by the oni Arataki Itto, who calls himself its "first and greatest head". Everyone in it means well, but its flyers, events, late-night music and accidents keep landing members in front of the Tenryou Commission. The Commission refuses to treat it as an official organisation. Deputy Kuki Shinobu gets the others out of trouble and handles the paperwork.

Leadership: Arataki Itto leads. He is brash and loud but honest and fiercely loyal, and he treats members with the respect of family.

Members: Besides Itto and Shinobu, the named members are Akira, Genta, Mamoru and Ushi, a young Akaushi bull.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the gang is active in Inazuma. It is led by Itto and Shinobu, still unrecognised by the Tenryou Commission, and still getting into minor trouble.

5.content:
Ayn Al-Ahmar (also: Ayn Al Ahmar, Ayn Al-Ahmar brigade): Ayn Al-Ahmar is a small Eremite mercenary brigade based in Port Ormos, whose members are fervent believers in King Deshret and hate Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. It is a subgroup of Deshret's Relics. Its leader Mizri bought a Divine Knowledge Capsule in a secret auction, convinced it held Deshret's power. Using it drove him mad, and the Matra took him away.

Leadership: Mizri leads the brigade. His followers call him "boss" and credit him with fervent devotion to King Deshret.

Members: Named members are Mizri (leader), Tariq and Tumart.

Goals: To bring King Deshret back. The brigade believes his power can be recovered, and that he will then punish Rukkhadevata's followers and the desert dwellers who forgot him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is known about the brigade's present state. Its leader was arrested in 3.0, and its parent group is described as dismantled.

6.content:
Beret Society (also: the Beret Society, Dougier's Beret Society): The Beret Society was a prisoners' club in the Fortress of Meropide in Fontaine. Its founder, Dougier, presented it as a way to help inmates turn over a new leaf, and its members wore berets as a badge of pride. In truth it was a scheme that ruled members through fear. Wriothesley and the Traveler exposed it during the Cerberus Chapter, and it was disbanded.

Status as of 7.1: Disbanded. Dougier was arrested and held in confinement after the Cerberus Chapter (4.1).

7.content: Black Serpent Knights (also: Black Serpent Knight, Windcutter, Rockbreaker Ax): Black Serpent Knights are one of the two forms of the cursed Royal Guard of Khaenri'ah, alongside the Shadowy Husks. They fight with greatswords (Windcutter) or dual axes (Rockbreaker Ax). Canon describes them as once-honoured knights of the realm whose reason and memory were stripped away by the curse. For the wider group, see the Black Serpents.

8.content:
Blazing Beasts (also: the Blazing Beasts, Dehya's brigade, Dehya's mercenary brigade): The Blazing Beasts are a small mercenary brigade of Eremites from Sumeru's desert. Their members are tightly bonded and loyal, and their best-known member is Dehya, the Flame-Mane. They take paid work as bodyguards and fighters. Dehya says outright that they are not a large group.

Leadership: Dehya is the face of the brigade. Her profile calls her a legend among the Eremites for her strength, passion and conscientiousness.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. No base is stated for the brigade, and it was last shown staying in Aaru Village (6.1 event).

9.content:
Bubu Pharmacy (also: Bùbǔ-lú, Not-Divining Hut): Bubu Pharmacy is the pharmacy and clinic that Liyue calls the finest in the land, set below Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor. Dr. Baizhu owns it and treats patients there. His apprentice Qiqi, an undead girl, gathers herbs, and the pharmacist Herbalist Gui makes up the medicines and minds the shop. It is especially busy during and after the Lantern Rite.

Structure: Baizhu owns and leads the pharmacy. Qiqi works as an apprentice and herb gatherer, and Herbalist Gui is the pharmacist behind the counter.

Leadership: Dr. Baizhu runs the pharmacy. He is courteous, says he treats every patient alike regardless of wealth or status, and is rarely seen without his white snake Changsheng.

Members: - Baizhu: owner and physician.
- Qiqi: apprentice and herb gatherer, a zombie raised by the adepti.
- Herbalist Gui: pharmacist and shopkeeper, still completing his training.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pharmacy is still operating under Baizhu in Liyue Harbor. No wiki page checked shows any change to it in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

10.content:
Champion Duelist (also: Champion Duelists, Fontaine's Champion Duelists, official Champion Duelist): The Champion Duelists are Fontaine's official trial fighters. A person on trial who wants to defend their honour can request a duel against one of them. The duelists are drawn from the country's best fighters, and the strongest at present is Clorinde. If the defendant wins, they are acquitted; if they lose, they simply stand trial.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Champion Duelists remain active in Fontaine. Clorinde is still the strongest and is no longer on a bodyguard post; she now works as a senior Game Master with the Tabletop Troupe and is travelling with Navia in Snezhnaya.

11.content: Chasm Exploration Team (also: The Chasm Exploration Team, Chasm exploration crew, Chasm Delvers): The Chasm Exploration Team is a small crew hired by Liyue's Ministry of Civil Affairs to look into the strange happenings in the Chasm, the mining region that was sealed off after a mysterious crystal appeared. They are the heart of the Chasm Delvers world-quest series, in which the Traveler helps them break the seal, set up camp in the Underground Mines and trace the dark mud to its source. Afterwards the team became an official part of Huishan Hall.

12.content:
Children of Echoes (also: Nanatzcayan, Nanatzcayan tribe, Children of Echoes tribe): The Children of Echoes, or Nanatzcayan, are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live in the canyons of Tequemecan Valley in eastern Natlan, where the ring of hammers and the tapping of gem hunters echo off the cliffs. They are miners, excavators, smiths and gem appraisers who work alongside drill-horned Tepetlisaurs, and they are known for their love of dance and rhythmic music. Their chief is Pacal. Kachina and Xilonen are the best-known members.

Leadership: Chief Pacal is a big, warm-hearted man who prefers looking after and supporting his people to managing the details of their lives. As a young man he hoped to be chosen by the Wayob, but he never received an Ancient Name. He took up eating to cope with stress, and once ate 71 servings of Glittering Gemstones in a contest. He made his peace with it, and he lives by the tribe's mantra: no one fights alone.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe lives on in Tequemecan Valley under Chief Pacal, rebuilding after the Abyss's invasion. Pacal stresses that the victory was real but temporary, and that the tribe must stay vigilant.

13.content:
Church of Favonius (also: Favonius Church, Mondstadt Church, the Church of Favonius, Church of the Anemo Archon): The Church of Favonius is Mondstadt's church of the Anemo Archon Barbatos, the nation's patron of freedom. Its clergy pray, run morning prayers and choir, help the sick and answer letters from believers at the Favonius Cathedral in Mondstadt City. The Knights of Favonius manage it, and the two institutions work side by side. Its Seneschal is Seamus Pegg, Cardinal of Daybreak.

Members: Notable members are Seamus Pegg (Seneschal), Cardinal Calvin, Dahlia (Deacon and Herald of Barbatos), Barbara (Deaconess and idol), Mother Maria and Sister Rosaria (who works alone).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Seamus Pegg is back in Mondstadt as Seneschal. The Church is peaceful and no Church-centred story content was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

14.content:
Collective of Plenty (also: Teteocan, Teteocan tribe, the Collective of Plenty): The Collective of Plenty, also called the Teteocan, is one of Natlan's six tribes. Its people farm the rich volcanic soil beside the Great Volcano of Tollan in Atocpan and live alongside Tatankasaurs, their bonded saurians. The tribe is known across Natlan for two things: the best fruit and vegetables in the nation, and a culture built around physical strength, from bodybuilding contests to wrestling. Its chief is Acatl, a cheerful masked wrestler.

Leadership: Chief Acatl is a tall, powerfully built man who always wears a horned wrestling mask. He is warm, relaxed about formalities and attentive to the tribe's young people, and he has long kept a concerned eye on Varesa.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is thriving under Chief Acatl. It survived the Abyss war, rebuilt, and fought off the Abyss Order's 5.7 attack.

15.content:
Communications Office (also: Heji Hall, Héjì-tīng, Liyue Communications Office): The Communications Office is one of the Eight Trades, the commercial sectors under the jurisdiction of the Liyue Qixing. It is the Hall in charge of transportation: moving goods and shipments around Liyue and arranging overseas shipping.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. No new story involving the Office was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

16.content: Conch Gang (also: the Conch Gang, Conch Gang kids): The Conch Gang is an informal band of stray children in Nasha Town, in Nod-Krai. Katya, the retired adventurer who runs the restaurant Speranza, feeds, houses and employs them while letting them live freely. The gang makes its own decisions by vote, and Speranza is its home base.

17.content:
Confrerie of Cabriere (also: Confrérie de Cabrière, Cabriere Confrerie): The Confrerie of Cabriere was a merchants' guild in Fontaine, founded and led by Marcel. Publicly it was one of the richest and most powerful trading guilds in the nation and a friendly sister body to the Spina di Rosula. In truth it was a front for Marcel's underground trade in Sinthe, which paid for his experiments. It was dissolved after Marcel was exposed in the 4.0 Archon Quest.

Status as of 7.1: Disbanded. The Confrerie ended when Marcel was exposed in 4.0.

key: Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty
18.content:
Corps of Thirty (also: the Corps of Thirty, Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty): The Corps of Thirty is the mercenary brigade that guards Sumeru City. It is not an official army. It is a permanently hired brigade of Eremites, kept on retainer by the Sumeru Akademiya, and its members wear teal-green scarves instead of the crimson ones of other Eremites. Its base is the Citadel of Regzar, and its commander is the Parchamdar, Rukh Shah.

Structure: A Parchamdar commands the Corps (the word means roughly "standard-bearer"). A Consultant serves beside the Parchamdar as a second, administrative leader.

Leadership: Rukh Shah is the Parchamdar. He is the youngest person ever to hold the post. The Consultant, Asfand, is a retired veteran who still advises him.

Members: Dehya, the "Flame-Mane", was once a member and is respected by the Corps. Other named members include Sido, the Swallow Sekkura, the logistics officer Yunus, Udad, the mercenaries Hakan and Farid, and Izem, a veteran now retired to the Puspa Cafe.

Relations: The Corps works for the Akademiya, has an uneasy relationship with other Eremites, and shares Sumeru City's security with the matra.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Corps of Thirty is still the working force of Sumeru City, based at the Citadel of Regzar under Rukh Shah.

19.content:
Courier's Longhouse (also: Couriers' Longhouse, Courier's Longhouse (Faction), Natlan couriers): The Courier's Longhouse is the courier agency of the Scions of the Canopy, the Natlan tribe of Coatepec Mountain. Its couriers carry letters and parcels. It accepts ordinary deliveries only, not anything extremely valuable, fragile or dangerous. It is run from a base in the Scions' settlement.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Longhouse is still operating at the Scions of the Canopy under its manager Michica.

20.content:
Court of Khaenri'ah (also: Court of Khaenriah, Khaenri'ahn Court, Khaenri'ah's court, Royal Court of Khaenri'ah): The Court of Khaenri'ah was the household of King Irmin, the last Vinster King, made up of his advisers, subordinates and others who served him in the underground kingdom. Its best-known member is the seer Vedrfolnir, called "The Visionary". It is chiefly remembered for the ceremony in which the Traveler's Sibling was named heir.

Status as of 7.1: The court no longer exists. It ended with the cataclysm about 500 years ago.

21.content:
Crimson Moon Dynasty (also: Red Moon Dynasty, Crimson Moon descendants, Crimson Moon bloodline): The Crimson Moon Dynasty is the earlier of the two known ruling dynasties of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom that fell in the cataclysm. It takes its name from the crimson moon that once shone over the realm. The dynasty is long gone, but some descendants survive and carry its Balemoon Bloodfire, most notably Arlecchino.

Members: No member of the dynasty's ruling house is named. Known descendants are Arlecchino and, in Khaenri'ah's last years, Tholindis, Frithr and Orlog.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the dynasty is long extinct as a ruling house. Its descendants include Arlecchino.

22.content:
Curatorium of Secrets (also: the Curatorium of Secrets, the Curatorium): The Curatorium of Secrets is an intelligence and commission agency in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, owned and run by Nefer. It takes commissions from the public, such as finding lost cats, tracking down people or things, and righting wrongs. It is also the public face of the underground Northern Intelligence Network. It follows a policy of strict neutrality toward every faction in Nod-Krai, and its only official employee is Jahoda.

Structure: Nefer is the owner and decides everything. Jahoda is the only official employee. Ashru, Nefer's cat, sits at the reception counter.

Leadership: Nefer, who came to Nod-Krai from Sumeru, owns the Curatorium and also heads the Northern Intelligence Network. She is calm, mercenary, and several moves ahead of whoever is in front of her.

Members: - Nefer: owner, head of the Network.
- Jahoda: the only official employee, a former Seahook Gang member whose life Nefer saved.
- Ashru: Nefer's black cat, the receptionist.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Curatorium is open and operating in Nasha Town. Nefer is back at its head, her sight having returned, and Jahoda still handles most of its commissions.

23.content:
Daydream Club (also: Daydream Club of Petrichor, the Daydream Club): The Daydream Club is a small group of inventors and researchers from Fontaine, centred on the town of Petrichor. Its members are united by their 'daydreams', ambitious ideas that other people call unrealistic. Known members include Garcia (Numbering Machine), Xavier (Film Kamera), Felix Yogue (a perpetual-energy machine), the brothers Mecantre and Babisse (a giant cannon), Grispan (phlogiston and thermal hypnosis) and Este. Their 'President' is a cat, Lady Grobel.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1 though scattered. The club's Petrichor members survived the mass dream and returned to their projects, and Grispan remains in Natlan.

24.content:
Druzhna (also: Druzhina, the Druzhna, Druzhna Guards, Winter Pact Corps): The Druzhna is Snezhnaya's personal guard of the Tsaritsa. It answers only to her, and most of its members are Vila, winged fae of the Snowland Fae. Besides protecting her, it is responsible for containing Shadow Realm breaches. Its headquarters is Druzhna HQ in the Everfrozen Earth area, and its Commander-in-chief is Vesna Strivozha.

Leadership: Vesna Strivozha, a Vila of House Strivozha, is Commander-in-chief. Her profile calls her the Tsaritsa's "keen blade", and she and the head housemaid Danica are both called the Tsaritsa's right hands and are often at her side.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Druzhna is active under Commander Vesna. It is short on hands for Shadow Realm work and is running the Special Recruitment Project to bring in volunteers.

25.content:
Eclipse Dynasty (also: Black Sun Dynasty, Dark Sun Dynasty, Blacksun Dynasty, the dark sun): The Eclipse Dynasty was the second and last known ruling dynasty of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom destroyed in the cataclysm 500 years ago. A dark sun stood as its emblem, replacing the earlier crimson moon. Its final ruler was the one-eyed King Irmin, and it fell with the kingdom.

Members: King Irmin, the last ruler; Dainsleif of the Royal Guard; and the Traveler's sibling, adopted into the royal house.

Status as of 7.1: The dynasty ended with Khaenri'ah's fall and no ruling house survives.

26.content:
Eight Trades (also: Bāmén, Eight Gates): The Eight Trades are eight commerce sectors that run Liyue's major industries, under the jurisdiction of the Liyue Qixing. Their divisions are called Halls or Offices. Canon names four: the Communications Office (transport), Huishan Hall (mining), Shenglu Hall (glazed ceramics) and Yinyuan Hall (salt).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Eight Trades remain Liyue's commercial administration under the Qixing. No new developments were found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

27.content:
Eleven Fatui Harbingers (also: Fatui Harbingers, Eleven Harbingers, Harbingers of the Fatui, the Eleven Fatui Harbingers): The Eleven Fatui Harbingers are the executive heads of Snezhnaya's Fatui. The Tsaritsa gives them god-like authority and Delusions, and each leads a division. The Director, Pierro ("The Jester"), leads them. In the early Archon Quest chapters they were sent abroad to collect the Archons' Gnoses.

Leadership: Pierro (Eftirvit), a former Khaenri'ahn royal mage, is the Director and was the first Harbinger.

Members: Roster as of 7.1: 1 Capitano (incapacitated, seat kept), 2 Dottore (dead), 3 Columbina (resigned), 4 Arlecchino, 5 Pulcinella, 6 Scaramouche (resigned, erased), 7 Sandrone, 8 Signora (dead), 9 Pantalone, 10 unknown, 11 Tartaglia (Childe). Seats without a note are active, as is the Director, Pierro.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 six are active: Pierro, Arlecchino, Pulcinella, Sandrone, Pantalone and Tartaglia. Capitano's body lies dormant on the Throne of the Primal Fire in Natlan.

28.content:
The Eremites (also: Eremites, Eremite, Eremite mercenaries, Eremite brigades): The Eremites are the desert mercenaries of Sumeru. They come from the Great Red Sand, whose ancient civilisations have collapsed, and they hire out their blades across Teyvat. Outsiders use "Eremites" as a blanket name for many separate brigades and tribes. Some are honourable, some are criminal, and some ignore the others entirely. They are the only authorised mercenary organisation in Sumeru, and many foreigners judge them as unscrupulous soldiers of fortune. The best-known members are Dehya of the Blazing Beasts and the Corps of Thirty who guard Sumeru City.

Status as of 7.1: Active in Sumeru as of 7.1, with the Corps of Thirty guarding the capital and brigades taking contracts across the desert.

29.content:
Fatui (also: Fatuus, the Fatui, Fatui of Snezhnaya): The Fatui (one member is a Fatuus; the name is Latin for "fools") are Snezhnaya's government, diplomatic corps and military in one body. They answer to the Tsaritsa, the Cryo Archon, who founded them 500 years ago with Pierro as their first member and Director. Under him the Eleven Fatui Harbingers each run a division. The Fatui are headquartered in Glupov, a fortress city inside Snezhnograd, and their emblem is the Palestar Banner. Abroad they present themselves as envoys of the Tsaritsa's goodwill, but most nations distrust them: in the Traveler's journey they took Gnoses from one Archon after another, using deceit, extortion, bribery and human experimentation along the way.

Structure: The Tsaritsa sits at the top. Below her, Director Pierro relays her appointments, assigns missions and convenes the Harbingers. Each Harbinger leads a division with personal subordinates, and below them are numbered companies and squads.

Leadership: **The Tsaritsa (Anastasya)** rules Snezhnaya directly, and the Fatui exist to carry out her will. **Pierro, "The Jester"**, is the Director of the Fatui, the first Harbinger and the Harbingers' leader. Each Harbinger takes a codename from Italian commedia dell'arte, a title and a rank number based on combat power.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fatui remain in power in Snezhnaya. Pierro mortally wounded Ronova with the new Eye of the Fatui but was left badly depleted. Ronova's curse is lifted, and Project Mistilteinn can resume.

30.content:
Fatui Internal Affairs (also: Okhranka, Fatui Internal Division, the Okhranka): Fatui Internal Affairs, also known as the Okhranka (Russian for "security"), is a special group within the Fatui that investigates misconduct among Fatui ranks. It answers to the Tsaritsa. Little else about it is known: canon names no members, leader or base.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is still the Tsaritsa's tool for judging Fatui misconduct. It has not appeared directly in any scene.

31.content:
Feiyun Commerce Guild (also: Feiyun Guild, Fēiyún Shānghuì, Flying Cloud Commerce Guild): The Feiyun Commerce Guild is a powerful trading guild in Liyue, run as a family business. It deals in silk, tea and printed books. Its best-known member is Xingqiu, the second son of the Guild Manager, a studious young man with a mischievous streak.

Structure: The Guild's leadership is the family: a retired great-grandfather who founded it, a grandfather who is patriarch, a father who manages it, and an elder son who is heir. Xingqiu is the second son.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guild is active, with Xingqiu still balancing its affairs against his wandering adventures. The wiki records no changes to it in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

32.content:
Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah (also: Five Sinners, the Five Sinners, Five Sinners of Khaenriah, Sinners of Khaenri'ah, Five Great Sinners): The Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah are five people who were once among Khaenri'ah's most admired, each the best in their field: "The Wise" Hroptatyr, "The Visionary" Vedrfolnir, "Gold" Rhinedottir, "The Foul" Surtalogi and the "Rächer of Solnari" Rerir. About 500 years ago, on the night they joined Dainsleif to storm the royal palace, they could not resist the call of the Abyss. They divided among themselves a world-shattering Abyssal power and became transcendent beings. When the cataclysm came, none of them defended their nation. Dainsleif, who fought beside them that night, has sworn he will never forgive them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 they act separately. Rhinedottir is the Ruler of Life, Surtalogi roams the stars, Rerir is trapped in the moon's reflection, and Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir are unaccounted for.

33.content:
Flower-Feather Clan (also: Tlalocan, the Flower-Feather tribe, Flower-Feather Clan settlement): The Flower-Feather Clan, whose older name is Tlalocan, is one of Natlan's six tribes. Its people live alongside the Qucusaurs, the proudest of the flying Saurians, and its elite flying squad patrols the skies on Qucusaur-back. The settlement sits among the cliffs of Quahuacan Cliff in northern Natlan, overlooking the ruins of Ochkanatlan. The current chief is Mutota. Its most famous member is Chasca, the Peacemaker who bears the Ancient Name Vuka.

Leadership: Chief Mutota is a scarred, grey-haired veteran who values patience and caution above bravado. He likes to remind people that scars are a badge of honour but also a record of mistakes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan has recovered from the Abyss invasion under Chief Mutota, and its flying trials have resumed. Allpa and her accomplices are in custody.

key: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering
Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering
34.content:
Fontaine Research Institute (also: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering): The Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, usually just "the Institute", is Fontaine's centre for the study of machines and energy. It was founded by the genius inventor Alain Guillotin, whose clockwork mechanisms and kinetic cores are still built in Fontaine's factories. Unlike Sumeru's Akademiya, it has no governing or teaching role. Its central laboratory was wrecked by an explosion during Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment, and the rebuilt Institute is better known for muddle and money trouble than for brilliance.

Leadership: Raimondo is the Senior Technician appointed to lead the Institute, and Choiseul is its administrative officer. Both took over the rebuilding after the explosion. Founding Director Alain Guillotin is long dead.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Institute works from the New Fontaine Research Institute, still active but troubled. After Sandrone's death in Nod-Krai, her core was delivered to the Institute, and she has since reawakened in Fontaine.

35.content:
Forest Rangers (also: the Forest Rangers, Forest Watchers, Vanara): The Forest Rangers are Sumeru's civil servants of the rainforest. They help travelers who are lost or in trouble, patrol the woods, watch the animals, and fight the spread of the Withering. Their main outpost is Gandharva Ville, "The City Above the Forest", in Avidya Forest. Higher-ranking members are called Forest Watchers and wear lighter green clothes. Tighnari is the Chief Officer, and Collei is an official ranger.

Structure: Two grades are seen: ordinary Forest Rangers and the higher-ranking Forest Watchers. Specialist roles include a doctor, a logistics chef and a search-and-rescue dog trainer.

Leadership: Tighnari is the Chief Officer of the Forest Rangers. He is an Avidya Forest Watcher and a botanist who graduated from Amurta.

Goals: Protect the rainforest and the people who pass through it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Forest Rangers still patrol Avidya Forest from Gandharva Ville. Collei is an official ranger, and Tighnari remains their Chief Officer.

36.content:
Four Winds (also: the Four Winds, Four Wind Guardians, Wolf of the North, Lion of the South, Dragon of the East, Falcon of the West, Lionfang Knight, Dandelion Knight): The Four Winds are four guardians of Mondstadt: the Wolf of the North, the Lion of the South, the Dragon of the East and the Falcon of the West. The Anemo Archon Barbatos entrusted them with the city's safety before he vanished a thousand years ago. Mondstadt once worshipped them and built temples to them. Today the worship has faded, and the titles live on mainly through the Knights of Favonius, the wolf spirit Boreas and the dragon Dvalin.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Four Winds are a fading tradition. Dvalin is again regarded as a guardian of Mondstadt; Boreas's spirit is in Wolvendom; Jean is Acting Grand Master and holds the Lion title; Varka is Grand Master and the Knight of Boreas. The Falcon is disputed.

37.content:
Frostmoon Scions (also: Moonchildren, Frostmoon Scion, Scions of the Frost Moon): The Frostmoon Scions, also called the Moonchildren, are an indigenous people of Nod-Krai descended from the fallen golden realm of Hyperborea. Their home is the Frostmoon Enclave on Hiisi Island. For centuries they have worshipped the Goddess of the Frost Moon, and in particular the Moon Maiden Kuutar, who was later revealed to be the former Fatui Harbinger Columbina. They are led by the Moonchanter Lauma. They are known for antlered crowns, silver blood, a gift for speaking with animals, vegetarian food, charity and deep suspicion of outsiders who threaten them.

Leadership: Lauma, the Moonchanter, is the spiritual leader, healer and voice of the Scions. She was chosen for the role at birth because she was born with an antler crown, silver blood and an extraordinary sensitivity to moonlight. Her people bring her every question, and senior members salute her as she passes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Scions still live in the Frostmoon Enclave under Lauma. Columbina lives among them as herself, not as a goddess to be petitioned. Older Scions still bow and keep their distance from her, but the children are curious.

38.content:
Fruity Order (also: the Fruity Order, Order of the Fruit, Five Great Operatives): The Fruity Order is a Treasure Hoarder group that operates in Fontaine and Nod-Krai. It is run by an unnamed boss, with Five Great Operatives who carry fruit and plant codenames, and several dozen other members. Betrayal is punishable by death. Its members claim the order exists to keep order and balance in the world. They are more eccentric than most Treasure Hoarders.

Status as of 7.1: Active but diminished: three of five operatives remain, and the boss is unnamed.

39.content:
Garde (also: Gardes, Fontaine Gardes, Garde officers, Captain of the Gardes): The Gardes are the uniformed security officers of Fontaine's Maison Gardiennage, the nation's law enforcement service. They patrol the Court of Fontaine, handle everyday public order, and share the patrol work with Gardemek meka. Their captain is Grosrochard. They are the standard-issue face of the law, as opposed to the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol or the Marechaussee Phantom.

Leadership: Grosrochard is the Captain of the Gardes. He is only ever mentioned: in Chevreuse's introduction he is the superior who wrote to her for the ninth time, asking her to be pickier about who joins the Special Patrol.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. The Gardes keep Fontaine's public order under Captain Grosrochard.

40.content:
Golden Troupe (also: Golden Troupe of Remuria, the Golden Troupe): The Golden Troupe was an order founded by Boethius, a Harmost of Remuria, from the survivors of the empire after its first fall. Its aim was to save Remuria and the Symphony (Phobos) so that music could unite the world in peace. It gathered in the Faded Castle, built music devices, studied spirit and fate, and used golems and sacrifice. It is long gone, but its remains lie under Petrichor in Fontaine.

Status as of 7.1: The troupe no longer exists. Its remains are in Petrichor and the Faded Castle, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found that changes this.

41.content:
Graffiti Alliance (also: the Alliance of graffiti artists, Natlan graffiti artists): The Graffiti Alliance is a group in Natlan that promotes the art and history of graffiti. Anyone can join, whatever their experience or style, and the Alliance gives new members free supplies and lessons. It is hundreds of years old and now has hundreds of members.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Alliance is active, with a headquarters and a couple of hundred members, and has money worries.

42.content:
Grand Alliance (also: the Grand Alliance, seven-tribe alliance): The Grand Alliance was the coalition of Natlan's seven tribes, created to build the new nation of Ochkanatlan under Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord. It began as an agreement between autonomous groups, but Och-Kan, growing obsessive, gathered the tribes' authority into his own hands. The Alliance ended in a civil war: by the wiki's reading, six tribes rose with the Scarlet-Eyed Youth and the seventh stood with Och-Kan. It is a historical organisation, long gone by the present day.

Status as of 7.1: The Grand Alliance has been defunct since the civil war. As of 7.1 it appears only as ancient history.

43.content:
Grand Narukami Shrine (also: Narukami Ooyashiro, the Grand Shrine): The Grand Narukami Shrine is Inazuma's chief religious organisation. It worships the Electro Archon and leads the faith of the Narukami people from the largest shrine in the nation, on the summit of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island, beside the ever-blooming Sacred Sakura. Its head is the Guuji, Yae Miko, a kitsune who is also the Shogun's friend and the owner of Yae Publishing House. Its shrine maidens wear white and red.

Leadership: Guuji Yae Miko leads the shrine. Worshippers and maidens call her "Lady Guuji" or "Lady Yae". She is solemn and mysterious in her ceremonial role and far more relaxed as head of her publishing house.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is active and Yae Miko is still Guuji. With the Sakoku Decree gone, worshippers now come to give thanks and pray for business and safe journeys.

44.content:
Guhua Clan (also: Guhua Brotherhood, Guhua Sect, Guhua School, Sect of Ancient Splendor): The Guhua Clan is a Liyue martial arts school that honours the wandering hero Guhua and teaches sword and spear. It was once famous across Liyue and beyond. Today only a few members remain, and its base, Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng, is falling apart. Xingqiu is its best-known member.

Members: Members the Traveler can meet include Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth at Wangshan Hall, Sun Yu and Little Que'er at Huaguang Stone Forest (until Sun Yu leaves), and Xingqiu. Former members include Chen the Sharp, a grilled-fish vendor in Liyue Harbor, and Zhiruo, a waitress.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guhua Clan is nearly extinct. A few members still keep Wangshan Hall, and no source shows a revival.

45.content:
Gunnhildr Clan (also: House Gunnhildr, Gunnhildr Family, the Gunnhildr Clan): The Gunnhildr Clan is Mondstadt's oldest family of knights. Its motto is "For Mondstadt, as always". Its roots go back to the priestess Gunnhildr, who stood with Barbatos against Decarabian, and the clan stayed loyal to the people through the age of the aristocracy. Many Knights of Favonius and Church clergy come from it. Jean is its best-known member today.

History: The clan traces itself to Gunnhildr, daughter of a nomadic clan leader who left Decarabian's city. She led her people alongside the wind spirit that became Barbatos and crowned him with laurels after Decarabian fell. In the aristocratic age the clan kept its oath to protect Mondstadt, and it sided with Vennessa's rebellion about 1,000 years ago.

Members: Jean Gunnhildr, Master of the Knights of Favonius, is the clan's heir and public face. Her mother is Frederica Gunnhildr, the Alder Knight. Her younger sister Barbara Pegg was born into the clan but left with their father, Seamus Pegg.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan remains in service. Jean is Acting Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

key: School of the Theory of Knowledge
46.content:
Haravatat (also: Haravatat Darshan, School of Semiotics, School of the Theory of Knowledge, Darshan of Semiotics): Haravatat is the Sumeru Akademiya's school of semiotics, the study of signs, meaning and language. It covers linguistics, ancient runes and the translation of old texts. Its colour is black, its crest shows a bull, and it is led by Sage Rushd. It is the smallest Darshan by enrolment, but it has produced Alhaitham, the Akademiya's Scribe, and the veteran scholar Faruzan.

Leadership: Rushd is the current Sage. He is the youngest of the sages and succeeded Khajeh after the Akademiya-Fatui plot collapsed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Rushd is the Sage and Alhaitham is Scribe. No Haravatat-specific story content was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

47.content:
Hexenzirkel (also: the Hexenzirkel, Circle of Witches): The Hexenzirkel is a secret society of extraordinarily powerful witches, "mages" in the game's English, founded by the adventurer Alice. Members are not chosen for virtue. Alice's main requirement was that a person be "interesting". They mostly pursue their own goals, meet at tea parties and keep a low profile. Its best-known members are Alice (Klee's mother), the seer Barbeloth (Mona's master), the alchemist Rhinedottir, and the voiceless former angel Nicole. It is allied with Mondstadt by a pact.

Members: - **Alice** (A): founder, a polymath adventurer and mother of Klee. She maintains the stability of Teyvat's borders.
- **Barbeloth** (B): a master astrologer and hydromancer, teacher of Mona.
- **Rhinedottir** (R): the Khaenri'ahn alchemist "Gold", one of the Five Sinners, who now holds the Ruler of Life's role.
- **Nicole** (N): a former angel, deprived of her voice, who guides others toward the truth.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Hexenzirkel is scattered. Alice is on duty at Teyvat's borders, Barbeloth is away in meditation, Nicole acts as guide and homework supervisor, Octavia is travelling, and Rhinedottir has been seen in Snezhnaya.

48.content:
High Table (also: the High Table, Fae Gang Federation, Fae Gang Federation's High Table, Vysokiy Stol): The High Table is an informal alliance of Snezhnaya's fae gangs. Its members live by a shared code called the Law, which limits how gangs treat ordinary people and one another. It was founded by the Domovoy Nikolay Izmaylov, the "Old Sire", and the surviving heroes who ended the Burner of Cities' rebellion. Since the Old Sire was killed by his adopted son, the alliance has been under strain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the High Table survives the Izmaylov incident, with Zmei acting as its voice. The Izmaylov gang has lost its leader, and the High Table must decide its future.

49.content:
Hiiragi Clan (also: Hiiragi family, House Hiiragi, Hiiragi-ke): The Hiiragi Clan is the family that heads the Kanjou Commission, Inazuma's finance, customs and border authority. Their estate stands in Ritou on Narukami Island. They serve the Raiden Shogun and have existed for at least 500 years. Their former head, Hiiragi Shinsuke, was jailed after a Fatui plot was exposed in 2.1, and his daughter Hiiragi Chisato now acts as head.

Leadership: The acting head is Hiiragi Chisato, daughter of the jailed Hiiragi Shinsuke.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Shinsuke remains in prison and Chisato acts as clan head.

50.content:
House of the Hearth (also: House of Hearth, the Hearth, Arlecchino's orphanage): The House of the Hearth is an orphanage run by Arlecchino, "The Knave" and Fourth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers. The children it raises call her "Father" and think of themselves as children of the Tsaritsa. Those judged to have potential are enlisted into the Fatui, often as spies or sleeper agents. Its best-known base is the Hotel Bouffes d'ete in the Court of Fontaine. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet are its best-known members. As of 7.1, Arlecchino has agreed with Pierro that the House will become independent of the Fatui and stop training children as spies.

Leadership: Arlecchino leads the House. Her birth name is Peruere; she was raised in it and took over by killing the previous director, Crucabena, whom the children called "Mother".

Members: Lyney (the Great Magician), his twin sister Lynette and Freminet, the diver, are the trio the Traveler knows best. All three are playable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the House is active and operating in Snezhnaya with Arlecchino. She has agreed with Pierro that it will become independent of the Fatui and stop training children as spies.

51.content:
House of Trubetskoy (also: House Trubetskoy, Trubetskoy family, Trubetskoy clan, Trubetskaya, Grand Duke Trubetskoy): The House of Trubetskoy is a noble house of Snezhnaya. Before the Cataclysm, 500 years ago, it held hereditary rights to the title of Grand Duke and to the governorship of Nod-Krai. Its current head is Euphrosiniya Ignatyevna Trubetskaya ("Euphie"), a Privy Councillor and reformer on the Snezhnograd Veche.

Leadership: Euphrosiniya heads the house today. Its named past heads are Prokhor Trubetskoy and his adoptive son Brahe.

History: Under Prokhor Trubetskoy and Brahe the house governed Nod-Krai from a palace that stood where the Lightkeepers' fortress Piramida now stands. After the Cataclysm Brahe gave up the land, and Nod-Krai became autonomous.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the house is active but without territory. Euphrosiniya heads it and works on the Veche to improve life for the poor of Zolnyy.

52.content:
House Solovyov (also: Solovyov family, Solovyov clan, Solovyov lineage, House of the Nightingale): House Solovyov was an old human noble family of Snezhnaya, loyal servants of the Belyi Tsar. Its emblem was the nightingale. It began as a family of spies, was raised to the gentry by the Tsar and sat among the fae at the Pale Star Court. Its best-known son is Solovei, the first Torchforger and founder of the Lightkeepers.

Members: Solovei, the younger son, later the Torchforger. His elder brother, never named, who inherited the nightingale emblem and was killed in the Tsar's service.

Status as of 7.1: No living Solovyovs are shown in canon through 7.1. The two named members are long dead.

53.content:
House Strivozha (also: Strivozha, the Strivozhas, Strivozha clan, Vila House Strivozha): House Strivozha is a famous noble house of the Vila, the winged fae of Snezhnaya. It was founded after the fall of Hyperborea under Grand Duchess Vaselisa von Strivozha, whom the Vila revere as a saint. Its people are known for sincerity, honour and loyalty, and for turning plants into perfumes and elixirs. In the present day its best-known member is Vesna, Commander-in-Chief of the Druzhna.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the house remains a respected Vila family. Its heir Vesna, Commander-in-Chief of the Druzhna, is playable.

54.content:
Huishan Hall (also: Huīshān-tīng, Bright Mountain Hall): Huishan Hall is one of the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing. It is in charge of the mining industry and of matters concerning the Chasm, the great mining region north of Liyue Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. No new story involving the Hall was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

55.content:
Hvergelmir (also: Hvergelmir institute, Hvergelmir research institute, Silent Source Facility): Hvergelmir was a secret research institute of the Pale Star Court in Snezhnaya, active before the Cataclysm 500 years ago. It was devoted to bio-alchemy and the study of the Shadow Realm and its Hyperborean ruins. The Belyi Tsar founded it and entrusted it to his adopted daughter Aksinya, whose public post was Court Jester. Its aim was to find "the stairway to the vacant seat in the court of the stars" and, concretely, to build a Proto-Man who would let the Tsar become the Primordial Human. It is long defunct, and its ruined halls lie beneath the Pale Crown Palace in the White Birch Snowgrave.

Status as of 7.1: Hvergelmir no longer exists. After the Cataclysm its leading members dispersed and its leader was trapped in the Shadow Realm. Its premises survive as the Ruined Hvergelmir.

56.content:
Imunlaukr Clan (also: the Imunlaukr, Tyrant of Imunlaukr): The Imunlaukr Clan was one of the founding clans of old Mondstadt, alongside the Gunnhildr and Lawrence clans. It descended from Imunlaukr, an outlander warrior, and became known for gifted fighters who fought hard and died young. In the dark age of the old aristocracy it turned tyrannical. Its bloodline is now gone.

Members: No individual clan member is named apart from the ancestor Imunlaukr, who gave the clan its name, and an unnamed "tyrant of Imunlaukr".

History: The clan came from Imunlaukr, whose descendants settled in what became Mondstadt. By the time Decarabian's rule ended it was known for brave, short-lived warriors. In the aristocratic age it grew tyrannical, and the Gunnhildr Clan broke with it. Today its line has died out.

Status as of 7.1: Extinct. The bloodline has vanished, and the clan is no longer mentioned in present-day Mondstadt.

57.content:
Inazuma Shogunate (also: Inazuma Bakufu, the Shogunate, Shogunate of Inazuma): The Inazuma Shogunate is the government of Inazuma. The Electro Archon heads it as the Raiden Shogun, also called the Almighty Shogun or "Her Excellency", from the castle of Tenshukaku in Inazuma City. Day-to-day rule belongs to the Tri-Commission: the Tenryou Commission (military and security), the Kanjou Commission (finance and borders) and the Yashiro Commission (shrines, festivals and culture), each led by a great clan. The Shogunate also commands the Shogun's Army. Its creed is the Shogun's ideal of Eternity.

Leadership: At the top is the Raiden Shogun. Under her, Kujou Kamaji is acting head of the Tenryou Commission's Kujou Clan and Kujou Sara is the general commanding its forces. Hiiragi Chisato is acting head of the Kanjou Commission's Hiiragi Clan, and Kamisato Ayato is the Yashiro Commissioner.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Shogunate is stable and open. The decrees are gone, the borders are open, the civil war is over, and Ei takes a more active role in rule with the puppet Shogun as her kagemusha.

58.content:
International Trade Association (also: Bankoku Shoukai, Ritou International Trade Association): The International Trade Association is a group of foreign merchants based in Ritou, the port island of Inazuma. It imports overseas goods such as Silk Flowers and gives practical help and shelter to outlanders who are new to Inazuma. Its president is Kurisu, a merchant from Fontaine. Under the Sakoku Decree, Ritou's Kanjou Commission treated its members harshly.

Leadership: Kurisu is the president. His real name is Christopher and he comes from Fontaine; he took the name Kurisu after arriving in Inazuma. He is courteous and patient, and he tells his members that outlanders must look after each other.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Association remains in business in Ritou under Kurisu. The Sakoku Decree is over, the former Kanjou Commissioner has been replaced, and the number of outlander merchants has grown.

59.content:
Izmaylov Family (also: the Izmaylovs, Izmaylov gang, Izmaylov (Family), Izmaylov fae gang): The Izmaylov family, or the Izmaylovs, are a Snezhnayan fae gang, the biggest and richest in the High Table. The Domovoy Nikolay Izmaylov, the "Old Sire", founded the gang, and his adopted son Vasiliy, the "Young Sire", inherited it. Vasiliy killed the Old Sire, pushed the gang into brutal debt collection to fund a plan to open the Shadow Realm, and died when the Traveler and the Luchkins stopped him. The gang is now leaderless.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Izmaylovs are leaderless. Vasiliy is dead, the Boneyard machine is destroyed, and the High Table is deciding the gang's future.

key: the Kamisato Clan of the Yashiro Commission
60.content:
Kamisato Clan (also: Kamisato family, House Kamisato, the Kamisato Clan of the Yashiro Commission, Kamisato-ke): The Kamisato Clan is one of the three great families of Inazuma under the Raiden Shogun. It leads the Yashiro Commission, the part of the Tri-Commission that oversees shrines, festivals and ceremony. The clan head is Kamisato Ayato, who handles government and politics. His younger sister Kamisato Ayaka, called the Shirasagi Himegimi, is the clan's public face, and Thoma is its chief retainer. The clan also commands the Shuumatsuban, a secret corps of ninja. It lives at the Kamisato Estate in Inazuma City.

Leadership: Kamisato Ayato leads the clan and the commission. He became clan head young, with the family weakened and rivals circling, and succeeded by tactics rather than force. He is courteous, shrewd and fond of tea, chess and calligraphy, and few people understand what he truly values.

Members: Kamisato Ayato (clan head and Yashiro Commissioner), Kamisato Ayaka (the clan's public face), and Thoma (chief retainer). Their late parents were the former clan head, who is unnamed, and Kamisato Kayo.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan still leads the Yashiro Commission and commands the Shuumatsuban from the Kamisato Estate. Ayato is clan head and Commissioner, Ayaka manages its public life, and Thoma serves as chief retainer. No later story has changed this.

61.content:
Kanjou Commission (also: Kanjou-bugyou, Kanjou Bugyou): The Kanjou Commission is the part of Inazuma's government that runs finances, customs and the borders. It is one of the three bodies of the Tri-Commission, serves the Raiden Shogun's Shogunate and is led by the Hiiragi Clan from Ritou, the port where foreigners are processed. During the Sakoku Decree it was feared for its strict rules and for abusing outsiders. After the Fatui plot in Inazuma was exposed, its Commissioner was jailed and his daughter Hiiragi Chisato took over as acting head.

Leadership: The acting head is Hiiragi Chisato, a young woman who runs the Hiiragi Estate in Ritou. Her father, Hiiragi Shinsuke, was Kanjou Commissioner until he was jailed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hiiragi Chisato acts as head of the Hiiragi Clan and the Commission. Her father remains imprisoned.

62.content:
Khaenri'ahn Dynasties (also: Dark Sun Dynasty, Black Sun Dynasty, Blacksun Dynasty, Khaenriahn Dynasties): Khaenri'ah, the subterranean kingdom that fell in the cataclysm 500 years ago, had two known ruling dynasties. The older Crimson Moon Dynasty is known almost only through a legend. The later Eclipse Dynasty was the last, and its final king, the Vinster King Irmin, pursued Abyssal power until the kingdom collapsed. The later house's Chinese name means "Black Sun Dynasty", and the legend that describes the change speaks of a "dark sun" replacing the crimson moon.

Status as of 7.1: Both dynasties are gone. Their legacy survives in the curse of the Khaenri'ahns, the Abyss Order and in Crimson Moon descendants such as Arlecchino.

63.content:
King Deshret's Priests (also: Desert Priests, Hermanubis Priest, priests of King Deshret, Heirs of the Burning Sun): King Deshret's Priests, also called the Desert Priests, were the priesthood who served the god-king of Sumeru's desert in his ancient kingdom. They wore the same style of head ornament as their head, Hermanubis, the Greatest of Sages and one of the king's Seven Pillars. They guarded the king's knowledge, and when forbidden knowledge ravaged the land they built the temples that held it back. Canon says little about them directly. No priest is shown alive in the present, and most of what is known comes from ruins, relics and one dying priest's recorded memory.

Leadership: Hermanubis was the guide of all the priests. Chosen from among the Tighnarians by King Deshret, he was a renowned sage and warrior known for being sincere, steady and kind.

Members: Only two members are named: Hermanubis as head, and Kasala as one of the last priests to serve under the king.

Status as of 7.1: The priesthood no longer exists as such. Its heritage continues through the Temple of Silence, now led by Sethos, and through descendants who claim it.

64.content:
Knights of Favonius (also: Ordo Favonius, Favonius Knights, the Knights of Favonius): The Knights of Favonius are Mondstadt's order of knights, founded about 1,000 years ago by Vennessa, with Barbatos' help, so that aristocrats could never rule again. They guard the city and its roads, keep order, make and enforce the law, and help manage the Church of Favonius. In practice they are Mondstadt's government. Their headquarters is in Mondstadt City.

Leadership: Grand Master Varka, the Knight of Boreas, is a huge, cheerful, famously strong man who hates paperwork. Jean Gunnhildr, the Master and Dandelion Knight, has governed as Acting Grand Master since Varka left on a long expedition half a year before the Traveler arrived.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the expedition has come home and Varka is back. He divides his time with the Favonius Keep in Nod-Krai, so Jean still runs daily affairs as Acting Grand Master.

65.content:
Komaniya Express (also: Komaniya, Komaniya Delivery): Komaniya Express is a well-known delivery company based in Inazuma. It is widely praised for punctual and safe delivery, and it has recently begun expanding its service overseas. Its best-known employee is Kirara, a nekomata and the company's Gold Level Courier.

Members: Kirara is the one employee canon names: a youkai (a nekomata) who loves her job and human society, and whose reputation has done much for the company.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Komaniya Express remains in business, now offering overseas delivery. Kirara handles all international orders.

66.content:
Korolevskiy Troupe (also: Korolevskiy Theater Troupe, Royal Troupe): The Korolevskiy Troupe is a performance company in Snezhnaya that specialises in opera, theatre, ballet and musical performance. It performs at the Korolevskiy Theater in Snezhnograd and is very popular, especially among the Fatui Harbingers and Mitya. Its two star performers are Odette, Prima Ballerina, and Vodyanitsa, Prima Donna. Both also have a hidden life beyond the stage.

Members: Odette, the Prima Ballerina, is calm, exacting and nearly expressionless on and off stage. Vodyanitsa, the Prima Donna, is a Water Imp (a Snowland fae) whose singing is said to carry an otherworldly allure; she is lively and outspoken.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the troupe is active at the Korolevskiy Theater in Snezhnograd. Odette and Vodyanitsa are both playable characters.

key: School of the Theory of Curiosities
67.content:
Kshahrewar (also: Kshahrewar Darshan, School of Technology, School of the Theory of Curiosities, Darshan of Technology): Kshahrewar is the Sumeru Akademiya's Darshan of technology. It covers mechanisms, architecture and puzzle-solving, and its colour is white with a lion on its crest. Its sage is Firnas. It built much of Sumeru City, but it has been underfunded since the loss of its greatest scholar, Pir Kavikavus. Its best-known graduate is the architect Kaveh, the Light of Kshahrewar.

Leadership: Firnas is the current Kshahrewar Sage. He reasons like an engineer, comparing crises to faulty machines. His predecessor was removed after the Akademiya-Fatui plot.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Firnas is the Sage. The Darshan remains underfunded, and no Kshahrewar-specific story was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

key: the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission
68.content:
Kujou Clan (also: Kujou family, House Kujou, the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission, Kujou-ke): The Kujou Clan is one of Inazuma's three great families and the head of the Tenryou Commission, the Raiden Shogun's executive arm for security and the army. It is regarded as the most loyal and powerful of the families supporting the Shogun's rule. During the Vision Hunt Decree the Kujou enforced the Shogun's order to seize Visions, through the general Kujou Sara. Its head, Kujou Takayuki, was then exposed as having worked with the Fatui for his own gain. His younger son Kujou Kamaji now leads the clan as acting head. Its estate stands next to Tenshukaku.

Leadership: Kujou Takayuki, the former head, is under house arrest. Kujou Kamaji is acting head and Tenryou Commissioner in his place. Masahito and Sara serve as generals.

Members: Kujou Takayuki (former head), Kujou Masahito (general), Kujou Kamaji (acting head), and Kujou Sara (adopted daughter, general). Kujou Shigeyori is the clan's founding-era ancestor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Kujou Clan still heads the Tenryou Commission under acting head Kamaji. Takayuki remains under house arrest awaiting punishment, and the Shogun has postponed any ruling on the clan. Masahito and Sara continue to lead the Shogun's forces.

69.content:
Lawrence Clan (also: House Lawrence, the Lawrence family, Lawrence noble family, Glacial Seal): The Lawrence Clan was the foremost noble house of Mondstadt's aristocracy. It began as hardy frontier survivors, grew into arrogant rulers and, about a thousand years ago, was deposed by Vennessa's rebellion and driven out of the city. Its descendants still live in Mondstadt, where the name draws hostility. The best-known member today is Eula, who left the clan's ways behind and serves in the Knights of Favonius.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan has no power and no known home. Eula serves as a Knights of Favonius captain, and many of her family regard her as a traitor.

70.content:
Legion of Soulblazers (also: Soulblazers, the Legion of Soulblazers, the Legion): The Legion of Soulblazers is a loose group of friends and pen pals led by Varesa of Natlan. Members come from several nations and began as a comic-book fan club. They are devoted to The Soulblazer Saga, a comic series about Natlan's fight against the Abyss, and treat its hero Fietena as a role model. Varesa says the group's real aim is to share life's joys and get rid of life's woes. It appears only in the limited-time event Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey (6.2).

Goals: The Legion exists to share life's joys and get rid of life's woes, in Varesa's words. The members read and discuss comics together, eat together and support one another.

Status as of 7.1: The Legion is last seen at the end of the 6.2 event, with Minnie free to travel and the group still in touch. It has not been mentioned again in anything checked through 7.1.

71.content:
Lightkeepers (also: the Lightkeepers, Lightkeeper, Ratniki, Warriors of the Nightingale): The Lightkeepers are Nod-Krai's militia against the Wild Hunt, the Abyssal host that has haunted the borderland since the Cataclysm. Solovei the Torchforger founded them about 500 years ago, and a royal edict from Snezhnaya made Nod-Krai an autonomous region under their protection. They are led by a Starshyna, currently Nikita, from the fortress-city of Piramida. Their fighters are called Ratniki, and every one of them carries an Oath Lantern. Their emblem is a nightingale holding a burning wick in its beak.

Leadership: Nikita, a middle-aged veteran the Ratniki fondly call "old man", is the current Starshyna. He took over about a decade ago when his predecessor Sigurd fell fighting the Wild Hunt.

History: When the Cataclysm struck about 500 years ago, Abyssal beasts overran Nod-Krai and the northern court could no longer protect its borderlands. Solovei, a Snezhnayan noble, came south, and with power lent by Aila, priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, drove the darkness back. The survivors raised a lighthouse in the mountains, and Solovei won a royal edict for Nod-Krai's autonomy in return for an oath of vigilance and sacrifice.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Lightkeepers are active under Starshyna Nikita, still understrength but recruiting again, and part of Nod-Krai's new League.

72.content:
Liyue Qixing (also: Qixing, Seven Stars of Liyue, the Liyue Qixing): The Liyue Qixing ("Seven Stars of Liyue") are a committee of seven business leaders who govern Liyue. Each is a magnate in their own field, and each holds a title named after a star of the Big Dipper. They meet at Yuehai Pavilion on Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor. For millennia they carried out the policies of Rex Lapis, the Geo Archon, and handled day-to-day government. Since his apparent death, which he staged, they have ruled Liyue without divine guidance. The best-known members are Ningguang, the Tianquan, and Keqing, the Yuheng.

Structure: The seven members are equal in rank, and each seat has its own area of responsibility. Ganyu, the General Secretary, has supported every generation of the Qixing.

Leadership: Ningguang, the Tianquan, is the Qixing's most public face. Keqing, the Yuheng, is known for hard work and for doubting reliance on the gods.

History: The Qixing formed after the Archon War, when Liyue's seven most successful merchants joined together. In the Liyue Archon Quest (1.0), after Rex Lapis' "death", they took full control of Liyue.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Qixing still govern Liyue. Ningguang and Keqing remain in office, and the rebuilt Jade Chamber floats above Liyue Harbor again.

73.content:
Lochknight (also: Lochknights, Lochknight order, Knights of the Lakelight): The Lochknights were the knights of Fontaine's legends: sworn, in silver armour, to protect the Oceanids (spirits born of pure water), the unpolluted springs and one another, and to resist the golden empire of Remuria. Their leader was Erinnyes. They are remembered less as a documented order than as a tale retold in plays, poems and films, and the Fontinalia Festival commemorates them.

Status as of 7.1: Defunct for centuries, existing now only as legend and festival.

74.content: Maison Cardinalice (also: Cardinal House): The Maison Cardinalice is one of the government offices of Fontaine, based in the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine. It oversees financial approvals and related administration, which in practice means reviewing and signing off on expense reports and salary payments from other offices.

75.content:
Maison Gardiennage (also: Maison Gardiennage of Fontaine, Fontaine law enforcement service, Fontainian law enforcement): The Maison Gardiennage is Fontaine's law enforcement service. Its main force is the Gardes, the uniformed officers, together with the Gardemeks, the clockwork meka that patrol with them. Two special branches sit beside them: the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, which arrests violent criminals, and the Marechaussee Phantom, a detective force that answers directly to Chief Justice Neuvillette. The service is based in the Court of Fontaine.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Maison Gardiennage continues to operate in the Court of Fontaine, with Chevreuse leading the Special Patrol and Neuvillette leading the Phantom.

76.content: Maison Gestion (also: Management House, Gestionnaires): The Maison Gestion is Fontaine's governmental body for document management and administrative tasks, based in the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine. Its employees are called Gestionnaires. It is known for paperwork, official stamps, endless approvals and an overcomplicated bureaucracy.

77.content:
Maison Ordalie (also: Ordalie, the Maison Ordalie): The Maison Ordalie is the part of Fontaine's government that runs the judicial system. It is led by the Chief Justice of Fontaine, called the Iudex, who is Neuvillette. It works from the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine, and its most public work is the trials held in the Opera Epiclese.

Leadership: The Iudex is Neuvillette, a figure of strict impartiality. He has been the only Iudex for a very long time, so long that people assume divine favour gave him an unusually long life.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Maison Ordalie still runs Fontaine's judicial system under Chief Justice Neuvillette, who has also effectively taken over the running of Fontaine from the Palais Mermonia.

78.content:
Marechaussee Phantom (also: Marechaussee Hunters, Maréchaussée Phantom): The Marechaussee Phantom is Fontaine's elite detective force, led by Chief Justice Neuvillette and made up largely of Melusines, whose sharp eyesight lets them notice more than most humans. It is a special branch of the Maison Gardiennage, based at the Palais Mermonia, and answers directly to Neuvillette. Its name comes from the Marechaussee Hunters, who once hunted monsters across Fontaine with special sword techniques.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Phantom is a detective force under Neuvillette, staffed mostly by Melusines. The Hunters exist as a tradition, with Clorinde as their best-known heir.

79.content:
Masters of the Night-Wind (also: Mictlan, Mictlan tribe, Night-Wind tribe): The Masters of the Night-Wind, also called Mictlan, are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live in a settlement perched on a foothill of the Tezcatepetonco Range. Of all the tribes they have the deepest bond with the Night Kingdom: their shamans commune with the Wayob, read fortunes, heal, bless weapons and keep watch over Natlan's Ley Lines and Phlogiston. Their chief is Biram, and their most famous member is the great shaman Citlali ("Granny Itztli").

Leadership: Biram, the current chief, is an enormous man (more than twice the Traveler's height) who wears an Iktomisaurus-like mask. He is progressive but unwilling to let change destroy tradition.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is intact under Chief Biram, after the Abyss war ended in 5.3. Citlali remains its great shaman, and Ororon still lives in the wild.

80.content:
Matra (also: the Matra, Matras, Akademiya disciplinary officers): The Matra are the disciplinary officers of the Sumeru Akademiya, its executive arm for academic integrity. They hunt down and sentence researchers guilty of serious offences such as plagiarism, fraud, bribery, misappropriation of funds and forbidden research. Their leader is the General Mahamatra, Cyno. Researchers fear them: a visit from the Matra almost never goes well.

Leadership: General Mahamatra Cyno commands the Matra. He is a young man of the desert who is stern, tireless and fond of jokes that nobody finds funny.

Status as of 7.1: Active under General Mahamatra Cyno as of 7.1.

81.content: Mighty Mythical Beasts (also: Mighty Mythical Beasts troupe, Gaming's Wushou troupe): The Mighty Mythical Beasts is a small Wushou dance troupe in Liyue. Gaming founded and leads it, and his aim is to make the beast dance a regular sight in Liyue Harbor. He promotes it by busking and by recommending it to the clients of the transport agency where he works as a guard. It has not yet had much professional success.

82.content:
Millelith (also: the Millelith, Millelith Brigade, Millelith soldiers, Millelith General Staff): The Millelith are Liyue's army and guard. They patrol the land, defend settlements against monsters and bandits, and answer to the Liyue Qixing. Their soldiers are famous for their skill with polearms, and their motto promises that evil will not prevail while they stand guard.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Millelith are active and still answer to the Liyue Qixing, with a General Staff and scenario-based training.

83.content:
Minghua Company (also: Minghua Bank, Minghua Trading Company): The Minghua Company, with its Minghua Bank, was the business of Gentry De'an in Liyue Harbor. A decade ago it was among the proudest firms on its street. Today the Bank is sold and the Company is languishing.

Leadership: Gentry De'an owned and managed both the Company and the Bank. No other officer is named.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Company still exists with failing business and De'an remains in Liyue Harbor. No newer developments were found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

84.content:
Ministry of Civil Affairs (also: Liyue Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, General Affairs Bureau): The Ministry of Civil Affairs is the working civil administration of Liyue, a body under the Liyue Qixing headquartered at Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor. It is made up of various departments and deals with the paperwork of a trading nation: permits, ports, taxes, festivals, information and public order. It can call on the Millelith when safety is at stake. Its staff are known for being overworked and curt.

Methods: It governs by permits and paperwork: business permits, exit permits, proficiency tests, tax and customs checks, port rent, bounties and watch lists.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Ministry is still Liyue's active administration. No major Ministry-led story event after the 2026 Lantern Rite was found in the checked sources.

85.content:
Mondstadt Aristocracy (also: Mondstadt's aristocracy, the Mondstadt aristocracy, Mondstadt nobility, Mondstadt nobles, Aristocratic Period, the aristocrats of Mondstadt): The Mondstadt Aristocracy was the class of noble clans who ruled Mondstadt after the fall of Decarabian's old city. They began as protectors of the people and, over centuries, became tyrants who enslaved commoners and staged gladiatorial games. The foremost clan, the Lawrences, ruled the city until Vennessa, an enslaved gladiator, led a rebellion with the help of Barbatos about a thousand years ago. Most nobles were exiled. The Knights of Favonius were founded so that nobles could never rule again.

Status as of 7.1: The aristocracy no longer exists as a ruling class. Descendants of its clans, especially the Lawrences, live in Mondstadt as ordinary citizens under suspicion.

86.content:
Mondstadt Wine Guild (also: Mondstadt Wine Appreciation Guild, the Wine Guild): The Mondstadt Wine Guild, also called the Mondstadt Wine Appreciation Guild, is the trade body of Mondstadt's wine industry. Its Executive Chairman is Elzer, who also manages affairs at Dawn Winery for Diluc. It is allied with the winery.

Leadership: Elzer is the guild's Executive Chairman, called Chief Executive in his own dialogue.

87.content:
Muratans (also: Muratan, the Muratans, the lost seventh tribe, the lost tribe): The Muratans were Natlanese exiles from the seventh tribe of the old Grand Alliance. After the civil war that ended Och-Kan's rule, one group of the defeated tribe accepted exile and wandered the land for generations before settling in Mondstadt. There they eventually forgot their heritage and the name Muratan. The best-known Muratan is Vennessa, the gladiator who led the rebellion against Mondstadt's aristocracy.

Status as of 7.1: No Muratan community is known to survive under that name as of 7.1. Their legacy lives on in Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius and its ideal of freedom.

88.content:
Mutual Aid Network (also: Mutual Aid Society, the Mutual Aid Network): The Mutual Aid Network is a small society of prisoners in the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's underwater prison. Vautrin, a former Garde captain exiled there, founded it about 400 years ago. Its members are mostly minor offenders who band together so that stronger inmates cannot push them around. Their badge is based on Vautrin's Medal of Peace.

Goals: Members help one another, work for justice and accept lawful judgment. They try to do something useful with their time inside and to face up to the crimes they committed.

Status as of 7.1: As of the 4.1 Diluvies Chapter, the Network is active in the Fortress of Meropide and canon records no later change.

89.content:
Narzissenkreuz Institute (also: Narzissenkreuz orphanage, the Institute (orphanage), Narcissus Cross Institute): The Narzissenkreuz Institute was an orphanage and school in Fontaine that raised orphans and the children of criminals. An Oceanid, Lyris, was its Director, and the retired admiral Basil Elton was its Vice Director. It scattered during the cataclysm 500 years ago, but its alumni, among them Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin, Rene and Jakob, went on to shape Fontaine for good and ill.

Status as of 7.1: Gone for 500 years. Its ruins are submerged beneath Annapausis.

90.content:
Narzissenkreuz Ordo (also: the Ordo, Ordo of Narzissenkreuz, Narcissus Cross Society): The Narzissenkreuz Ordo was a Fontainian secret society founded by Rene de Petrichor and his adoptive brother Jakob Ingold. Convinced a second flood would end the world, it sought to fuse countless wills into one being able to survive it. Its base was the Tower of Ipsissimus. It is defunct as of 4.2.

Structure: The Master, Narzissenkreuz, led; Jakob Ingold served as his right hand. Members held clearance levels 1 to 4.

Leadership: Narzissenkreuz, the Master, is Rene after he dissolved himself and was reborn in a body drawn from the Oceanid Lyris, Carter Scherbius and Alain's watch. Jakob built him.

Members: Rene and Jakob (founders), the Master, the Oceanid Lyris ("Red Empress"), Caterpillar, and scholars and patrons of lower levels.

Goals: To outlive the end of the world. Rene's "world-formula" predicted a flood, and the Ordo meant to merge many wills into a Descender-like being.

Status as of 7.1: Defunct as of 7.1. The Master lies at rest in Annapausis, Jakob was lost in the Doomsday Clock's collapse and the tower has sunk.

91.content:
Northern Intelligence Network (also: the intelligence network, the black market of intel): The Northern Intelligence Network is an underground organisation in Nod-Krai that works as a forum, or in Varka's words a black market, for intelligence. Well-connected people trade what they know for payment, with no real rules or regulations. It is run by Nefer, its current representative, and sells to clients of any faction across the world, though it has no foothold in Liyue.

Structure: Loosely structured, with no rules or regulations to speak of. It is made of volunteers, informants and paying clients who deal with one another through Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets.

Leadership: Nefer, the owner of the Curatorium of Secrets, is the Network's current head and representative.

Members: Nefer is the head. Jahoda is the only official employee. Diluc is a contact with the codename "Owl". Yelan and Varka are customers.

History: The Network was first hinted at in Diluc's fourth Character Story as a vast underground intelligence network in the north. It was named in 6.1 and became central to the Song of the Welkin Moon story, in which Varka brought the heroes to a Network contact hub.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Network is active under Nefer, based in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai.

92.content:
Northland Bank (also: Banque du Nord, Northland Bank branch, Regrator's bank): The Northland Bank is a Snezhnayan bank with branches across Teyvat. Its president is Pantalone, "Regrator", the Ninth Fatui Harbinger. The Fatui use funds from the Bank when operating outside Snezhnaya and sometimes use its branches as bases. Its main branch and the underground vaults beneath it are in Snezhnograd. Visible branches stand in Liyue Harbor, Nasha Town in Nod-Krai and the Court of Fontaine, and a branch was being opened in Sumeru City.

Leadership: Pantalone founded the Bank shortly after becoming a Harbinger and has been president since. He also oversees Snezhnaya's finances.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bank operates normally with Pantalone as president. The Seals of Life it stored in Snezhnograd were returned to their donors at the end of the 7.1 Archon Quest, and the Bank is negotiating compensation for damaged or missing seals.

93.content:
Order of Skeptics (also: Shamaniyya, Nagarjunites, the Skeptics, Vijnanapati, Nasuraia): The Order of Skeptics, which the Akademiya calls the Nagarjunites, is a small group of scholars living in the Girdle of the Sands in southern Sumeru. They descend from an Akademiya Darshan that came to the desert 500 years ago, during the cataclysm, and helped the Pari purify the Harvisptokhm. They have long since cut ties with the Akademiya and are rarely acknowledged. Their creed is the "transmission of knowledge at all costs" and that "conflict is the natural order of Teyvat". In 3.6 their leader Nasejuna turned on the Pari and tried to take the Great Songs of Khvarena for the Abyss Order.

Leadership: Leaders are called Nasuraia or Vijnanapati. Nagarjuna, a one-armed sage, is counted as the first. The last, Nasejuna, fled in 3.6, and the order is currently leaderless.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the order has no leader, and its few members remain in the Girdle of the Sands. No newer Skeptics content was found after the 3.6 Khvarena of Good and Evil chapter.

94.content:
Pale Star Court (also: Pale Star's royal court, Pale Star Royal Court): The Pale Star Court was the empire and royal court of the Belyi Tsar (White Tsar), whose personal name was Monomakh Snezhnyi. He united the rival Snowland Fae kingdoms of the far north under one crown, and his realm is the direct ancestor of the nation of Snezhnaya. Later texts also use the name for his regime as the first Cryo Archon. It ended when he fell in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago, and Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, took his place.

Leadership: The Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi, founded and ruled the court. He claimed a "sacred bloodline" that set him above other fae, though the fae chronicle suggests the claim was a way to appear legitimate. He later became the first Cryo Archon and God of Love.

Status as of 7.1: The court no longer exists as a state. It ended with the Belyi Tsar's death roughly 500 years ago.

95.content:
People of the Springs (also: Meztli, Meztli tribe, the People of the Springs): The People of the Springs (Meztli) are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live by the hot springs and coast of Toyac Springs, in a settlement also called "People of the Springs". Their Saurian partners are the swimming Koholasaurs. They are famous as guides, mapmakers, surfers and hosts, and their land is the tribe most popular with visitors. Their current chief is Amina.
