Mualani, a guide and surf-shop owner, bears the tribe's hero Ancient Name, Umoja ("unity").

Leadership: Chief Amina leads the tribe. She is young, full of ideas and determined to take her job seriously. She took over after her grandfather died, and the late warrior Atea was her mentor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and rebuilding after the Abyss war, with Amina as chief.

96.content:
Ragnvindr Clan (also: Ragnvindr Family, House Ragnvindr, the Ragnvindr Clan): The Ragnvindr Clan is a rich and respected Mondstadt family who own the Dawn Winery, the city's premier winery. It takes its name from Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight, who sided with Vennessa against the aristocracy about 1,000 years ago. It is one of the two known noble houses that were not exiled when the aristocracy fell. Its present head is Diluc.

Structure: Diluc is head of the family and owner of the winery. His adopted brother Kaeya belongs to it by adoption.

History: The family's namesake Ragnvindr was a young nobleman and knight's squire in the aristocratic age who joined Vennessa's rebellion. Later generations ran the winery. Four years before the main story Crepus died, Diluc left the Knights of Favonius, and he returned to take over the winery.

Members: Diluc Ragnvindr is the head. Kaeya, adopted by Crepus, is Diluc's estranged brother and is Cavalry Captain of the Knights. Crepus is dead. The founder-figure is Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Diluc runs the winery, remains outside the Knights and keeps up his night patrols. Kaeya remains a Knights captain. No new family developments were found for 6.7 to 7.1.

97.content:
Rokot (also: the Rokot, Рокот): The Rokot is a covert popular movement in Snezhnaya that serves "the common people" and works against Project Stuzha, the Tsaritsa's grand scheme that has strained the country's supply of Kresnik Kristall. Members use codenames and mostly do not know who one another are. The movement avoids violence and tries to help the public by quieter means. The Fatui keep watch on it and count it as an opponent. Alyosha, Vodyanitsa and Odette are members, and the Traveler joins in the Archon Quest.

Members: Alyosha (a hunter from Sretomorozsk), Vodyanitsa (Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe) and Odette (Prima Ballerina of the troupe and a Fatuus), plus the Traveler. Trapeznikov, a research-minded NPC, also belongs.

Goals: The Rokot wants to improve ordinary people's lives and to see Project Stuzha ended, which is why it opposes the plan's backers and, on occasion, the Tsaritsa herself.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Rokot is active. Its president remains unnamed, the codename Lelek is retired, and its members continue everyday good works in Snezhnaya.

98.content:
Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya (also: Energy Commission, Snezhnaya Energy Commission, Royal Energy Commission): The Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya, often just the Energy Commission, is the state organisation responsible for Snezhnaya's energy upkeep. It maintains the Kresnik's Torches, the furnaces that make Snezhnayan cities habitable, and manages the transport and use of Kresnik Kristall, the ore the torches burn. It answers to Zapolyarny Palace.

Leadership: The Commission has been led by an Acting Chair, Zarechnaya, since its long-time President Izmaylov, an old Domovoy, died. She was sent from Zapolyarny Palace to keep the Commission running until a permanent chair is found.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Commission still operates under an Acting Chair, Zarechnaya. Its president Izmaylov is dead.

99.content:
Rtawahist (also: Rtawahist Darshan, School of Illuminationism, the Rtawahist school): Rtawahist is one of the six Darshans, the great schools of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is illuminationism, the study of the stars, including astronomy and astrology. Its members believe the sky reflects truth and that the stars write people's destinies. Its school colour is blue, and its crest shows an elephant-like mascot.

Leadership: Shakir is the current Rtawahist sage. Azar was the Darshan's sage and the Akademiya's Grand Sage before he was removed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Rtawahist is led by Shakir. Azar remains in exile in the Avidya Forest, and no new Rtawahist story was found after Chapter III.

100.content:
Saurian Relics Association (also: Saurian Relics Association (Faction), the Saurian Relics Association): The Saurian Relics Association is a Natlan organisation that gathers, appraises and studies relics left by the ancient saurians. It was founded by Copan, a scholar of the Collective of Plenty. It is poorly funded and of uneven reputation. Its branch at the Chuwen Fair in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame has become a souvenir counter, a notice board and, in the manager's words, a giant flea market.

Structure: Researchers, excavators, investigators and shop staff, with no named president today.

Goals: To collect and catalogue saurian-era relics and keep them as part of Natlan's heritage.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1 and still short of money.

101.content:
Schwanenritter (also: Schwanenritters, Swan Knights, heroes of Dahri): The Schwanenritter ("Swan Knights" in German) were an order of Khaenri'ahn knights who fought the Abyssal monsters when the cataclysm struck Khaenri'ah about 500 years ago. Led by Knight Marshal Anfortas, they escorted able-bodied survivors up into Sumeru and held the line with machines called Ruin Golems. Their known members all fell, one by one, in a foreign land. Nagarjuna's scholars, the future Order of Skeptics, honoured them as the "heroes of Dahri".

Leadership: Knight Marshal Anfortas led the order and, when King Irmin was left "indisposed" by the crisis, proclaimed himself Marshal Regent and led the Regnum Concilium Ultimum, the Final Kingdom Council.

Status as of 7.1: The order no longer exists. Its last known member, Anfortas, is presumed dead.

102.content:
Scions of the Canopy (also: Huitztlan, Huitztlan tribe, the Scions of the Canopy, Scion of the Canopy): The Scions of the Canopy, also called the Huitztlan, are one of the six tribes of Natlan. They live in a village of huge trees and platforms hung by ropes off the cliffs of Coatepec Mountain, alongside their saurian partners, the Dendro Yumkasaurs. They are known as couriers, hunters and explorers, and they love extreme sports. Their chief is Wayna. The tribe's best-known member today is the Saurian Hunter Kinich, and the Pyro Archon Mavuika was born among them about 500 years ago.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is back in its cliff village under Chief Wayna, rebuilding after the 5.1 Abyss invasion killed many of its people.

103.content:
Seahook Gang (also: the Seahooks, the original Seahook crew): The Seahook Gang was a gang of thieves and bandits that once held real sway in Nod-Krai, centred on Nasha Town. It no longer exists in its original form: its boss was killed by his own men and the rest scattered. Today the name is used by impostors who want its intimidating reputation. The best-known former member is Jahoda, now an employee of Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets.

Status as of 7.1: The original gang is gone. Impostors still use the name in Nod-Krai, and a few ex-members are said to have crossed to Fontaine.

104.content:
Seven Pillars (also: Seven Sages, seven monk-kings, King Deshret's Seven Pillars, Seven Pillars of King Deshret, Seven Pillars of Al-Ahmar): The Seven Pillars, also called the Seven Sages or seven monk-kings, were the chief retainers of King Deshret (Al-Ahmar), the desert god-king of ancient Sumeru. He gave them his power, and they served as his "pyramid of authority". Three were gods he had defeated: Heryshaf the Goat King, Sobek the Crocodile King and Thoth the Ibis King. Bennu and Shesepankh were intelligent constructs he built, and Hermanubis was a human sage raised to be his familiar. The seventh, the Dendro Dragon Apep, was named a Pillar by Deshret but never accepted it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Pillars no longer act as an order. Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth are free, and Bennu and Shesepankh are awake. Hermanubis is gone, and Apep keeps her distance.

105.content:
Shenglu Hall (also: Shenglu Chamber): Shenglu Hall governs Liyue's glazed ceramics industry. It is one of the Eight Trades, the commerce sectors that answer to the Liyue Qixing. Its members are said to descend from tribes that lived near the Chasm long before Rex Lapis arrived, and the trade depends on materials from the Chasm.

Leadership: Miss Ruoyu is the Hall's industry representative.

106.content:
Shogun's Army (also: Shogunate Army, Bakufu Army, Shogunate forces, Inazuma Shogunate army, Army of the Shogun): The Shogun's Army is the military of the Raiden Shogun, Ei, and of the Inazuma Shogunate. It keeps peace and order across Inazuma and is divided among the three bodies of the Tri-Commission. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, provides the main fighting force. The Kanjou Commission handles border security, and the Yashiro Commission handles protection of shrines, festivals and public events. Some members serve the Shogun directly. Its soldiers are also called Shogunate Samurai, and their ranks are modelled on those of the historical Tokugawa shogunate.

Leadership: The Raiden Shogun, Ei, is the army's head, and the Kujou Clan commands it in her name through the Tenryou Commission. Kujou Sara, an adopted tengu, and Kujou Masahito are its two Generals.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the army remains Inazuma's military, but under a more open, post-decree Shogunate. The Vision Hunt and Sakoku decrees are gone and the ceasefire with the Watatsumi Army holds.

107.content:
Shuumatsuban (also: Shiyuumatsu-Ban, Shuumatsu-ban, the Shuumatsuban): The Shuumatsuban is a secret unit of ninja in Inazuma, part of the Yashiro Commission's hidden side and answerable to the head of the Kamisato Clan, currently Kamisato Ayato. Most Inazumans do not know it exists. It takes on matters that are awkward for the higher-ups to handle openly. Its best-known member is Sayu, a sleepy young ninja who is far better at hiding from work than doing it.

Structure: There is no public structure. The unit reports to the Kamisato Clan head, who is also the Yashiro Commissioner. Beneath him are ninja and support staff, with most identities classified.

Members: Sayu is the best-known ninja. Other named ninja include Hisashi, Gaumaru and the ninken Inu Shoushou. Most members are orphans raised from a young age by the unit.

108.content:
Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau (also: Transport Bureau, Railway Transport Bureau, Chicota, Snezhnaya Imperial Railway Transport Bureau, Transportation Bureau): The Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau, usually called the Transport Bureau and sometimes Chicota, is the organisation in charge of Snezhnaya's railway system. Its staff run Central Station in Snezhnograd and the trains that cross the snowfields. The wiki also notes an uncommon translation as the Snezhnaya Imperial Railway Transport Bureau.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bureau remains active, with staff at Central Station and on trains. No Bureau-centred story was found in the sources checked for 7.0 and 7.1.

109.content:
Snezhnograd Veche (also: the Veche, Veche, Snezhnogradskoye Veche): The Snezhnograd Veche (Snezhnogradskoye Veche, "the Veche") is Snezhnaya's legislative assembly. It sits in the Veche State Hall in Snezhnograd and decides matters by majority vote in sessions chaired by a Speaker. The Tsaritsa founded it to take over the administration once the fae princes' rule ended. The Speaker is the Fatui Harbinger Pulcinella, and the Fatui steer most of its decisions.

Leadership: The Speaker is Pulcinella, the Fifth Fatui Harbinger, "the Rooster", who is also Mayor of Snezhnograd and of Glupov. Members call him "Lord Rooster" at sessions.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Veche continues to meet under Speaker Pulcinella. Project Stuzha was kept going in 7.0, then paused.

110.content:
Spantamad (also: Spantamad Darshan, School of Elementalism, the Spantamad school): Spantamad is one of the six Darshans of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is elementalism, the study of the elements and the elemental reactions and changes that follow from them, with related work in Ley Line studies and alchemy. Its school colour is red. Because Ley Line research needs fieldwork, it has the most Driyosh, the Akademiya's traveling scholars. Lisa of the Knights of Favonius and Cyno both studied here.

Leadership: Alkindi is the current Spantamad sage. Cyrus, a retired professor, is a former sage.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Spantamad is led by Alkindi. No new Spantamad story was found for 6.x-7.1.

111.content:
Spina di Rosula (also: Spina, the Spina, Thorny Rose Association): The Spina di Rosula is a Fontainian organisation that helps ordinary people and takes on the problems the Gardes cannot or will not handle. Callas founded it, and his daughter Navia is now its President and "Boss". Its members work from Fleuve Cendre, the undercity beneath the Court of Fontaine, and from Poisson. Officially it describes itself as law-abiding and citizen-focused, and it cooperates with the authorities where needed. Navia's own description is "a business partner" that helps with any problem, using the velvet glove or the iron fist as the case demands.

Leadership: Navia is the second President. She took the post from her father Callas, who founded the Spina, after his death. She is cheerful, tireless and theatrical, and her own people treat her as the one to bring problems to.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Spina di Rosula is active under President Navia, with Florent as Senior Advisor and Poisson's reconstruction under way.

112.content:
Sumeru Akademiya (also: Akademiya of Sumeru, Six Darshans): The Sumeru Akademiya is both Sumeru's government and the most prestigious academy in Teyvat. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata founded it, and its main building, the Akademiya, sits on the Divine Tree above Sumeru City. Its scholars are divided into six Darshans (schools), each led by a Sage, and one Sage serves as Grand Sage. It runs Sumeru's day-to-day affairs, from trade and ports to hospitals and law. The old sages under Grand Sage Azar confined the Dendro Archon and plotted with the Fatui to make a new god. Since their fall, the Akademiya has served Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), and its current Grand Sage is Naphis.

Leadership: Grand Sage Naphis, the Amurta Sage, is a man of integrity with a legendary temper. He was Tighnari's teacher. Lesser Lord Kusanali now guides the Akademiya directly.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Akademiya is led by Grand Sage Naphis and five other sages, under Nahida's guidance. After the 6.6 Irminsul crisis, people have returned to Sumeru City and are rebuilding.

key: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
113.comment: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
113.content: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency (also: Secure Transport Agency, Sword and Strongbox Agency): The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency is a guild of guards for hire based at Yilong Wharf in Liyue. Its guards escort valuable cargo and lone travellers so that bandits and wild beasts cannot rob them. It is a sub-organization of the Communications Office, which handles shipments and transport across Liyue. Its best-known guard is Gaming.

114.content:
Tanit (also: Tanit tribe, Tanit Tribe, the Tanit, Tanit Eremites): The Tanit were a nomadic Eremite tribe of Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth, matrilineal and led by a Matriarch and Nine Elders. They worshipped the Goddess of Flowers, traded in crocodile goods, spices and oils, and raised stolen or lost children as Falcons. Their last camp, the Tanit Camps, lay on the desert's southern edge. The tribe was destroyed in the events of Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...

Status as of 7.1: The Tanit are gone. Babel is dead and the tribe was destroyed by Jeht and the Traveler, leaving only a few survivors. The Tanit Camps are now empty.

115.content:
Tenryou Commission (also: Tenryou Commissioner, Tenryou-bugyou, Tenryou Bugyou): The Tenryou Commission is the Raiden Shogun's executive arm in Inazuma: it keeps public order, commands the military and police, and enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. It is one of the three bodies of the Tri-Commission and is led by the Kujou Clan. After the Fatui plot in Inazuma was exposed, its Commissioner Kujou Takayuki was removed, and his son Kujou Kamaji now leads it as acting head.

Leadership: The Commission is led by Kujou Kamaji, an official who fills in as Proxy Clan Head. Generals Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito command its forces. Sara is a tengu adopted into the Kujou Clan.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Kamaji acts as head of the Kujou Clan and the Commission. Takayuki remains under house arrest.

116.content: The Black Serpents (also: Black Serpents, Shadowy Husks, Shadowy Husk, Royal Guard of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ahn Royal Guard): The Black Serpents are what is left of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard, the knights who served under Captain Dainsleif before the nation fell. The curse on Khaenri'ah wore away their minds and memories. The Adventurer Handbook says only a will to "fight for something, someone, and some matter" remains. Depending on how worn they are, they are called Shadowy Husks or Black Serpent Knights. Outside quests they appear as elite enemies in the Chasm's underground mines and in the Spiral Abyss.

117.content:
The Crux (also: Crux Fleet, the Crux Fleet, Crux): The Crux is an armed fleet based in Liyue Harbor and led by Captain Beidou. Its sailors carry cargo across seas no ordinary merchant would risk, fight sea monsters and pirates, and are famous throughout Liyue for daring voyages and rich bounties. Its flagship is the Alcor. Everything it does is approved by the Qixing, in the words of Beidou's profile, "more or less".

Leadership: Captain Beidou, the Uncrowned Lord of the Ocean, established and leads the Crux. When she goes ashore for business, Chief Mate Juza minds the Alcor and the crew, as he tells visitors himself.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Crux is active and still led by Beidou. Juza keeps the Alcor, which is anchored off Guyun Stone Forest while Beidou is in the city.

118.content:
The Steambird (also: Steambird, The Steambird newspaper, Steambird Newspaper): The Steambird is the main newspaper of the Court of Fontaine, read across Teyvat. Its office stands in Quartier Narbonnais, and its Chief Editor is Euphrasie. Its best-known reporter is Charlotte. Besides news it runs a reader-submission column, and it organises the La Verite Prize for journalism.

Leadership: Euphrasie is the Chief Editor. She runs the paper, assigns and recalls reporters such as Charlotte, and deals with the complaints and threats that follow. She speaks formally and with dry humour.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 The Steambird is active in the Court of Fontaine with Euphrasie as Chief Editor. Sir Arthur, Charlotte and the columns continue as before.

119.content:
Treasure Hoarders (also: Treasure Hoarder, the Treasure Hoarders): The Treasure Hoarders are a gang of bandits who hunt treasure in ruins and domains all over Teyvat and get rough with bystanders who happen to be nearby. They are poorly organised because the groups are so far apart. The gang's official description credits a founder called Reed Miller, who called it "an organization of mutual cooperation." The group is said to have originated in Nod-Krai. Members join over crime or lack of steady income, and they tend to burn through loot fast and stay poor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Treasure Hoarders remain active, scattered local gangs across every nation. No 7.0-7.1 story content about them was found. Their last major appearance is in the Nod-Krai content: the Reed Miller legend, Hiljetta and the Proofs of the Cognoscenti (6.3).

120.content:
Tri-Commission (also: Sanbugyou, San-bugyou, Three Commissions, Three Commissioners): The Tri-Commission (Sanbugyou, "Three Commissioners") is the collective name for the three organisations that run Inazuma's government under the Raiden Shogun. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, handles security and the military. The Kanjou Commission, led by the Hiiragi Clan, handles finance, customs and the borders. The Yashiro Commission, led by the Kamisato Clan, handles shrines, festivals and ceremonies. An Inazuman in Liyue compares them to Liyue's Qixing and Eight Trades and to the Knights of Favonius.

Leadership: The Raiden Shogun rules over the three. The Kujou, Hiiragi and Kamisato clans lead the Tenryou, Kanjou and Yashiro Commissions. Kamisato Ayato leads the Yashiro Commission, which was untouched by the Fatui scandal.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tri-Commission stands, with Ayato leading the Yashiro Commission and acting heads Kamaji and Chisato leading the Tenryou and Kanjou.

121.content:
Universitas Magistrorum (also: the Universitas, University of the Magisters): The Universitas Magistrorum was a Khaenri'ahn institute of learning whose members worked in astrology, alchemy and other arts. It was directly subordinate to the Vinster King Irmin and held real influence in the kingdom. Before the cataclysm it was led by President Hroptatyr, "The Wise", with Eftirvit, later called Pierro, as Vice-President. After Irmin became obsessed with the Abyss, it turned into a major centre of Abyssal research. What became of it after the kingdom fell 500 years ago is not stated.

Status as of 7.1: The Universitas Magistrorum no longer exists as a known body. Its two leaders live on as the Fatui Director Pierro and as Hroptatyr, a Sinner of Khaenri'ah whose memory was glimpsed in 7.1. Canon does not say whether the institute itself survived the cataclysm.

122.content:
Vahumana (also: Vahumana Darshan, School of Aetiology, Darshan of Aetiology, Vahumana scholars): Vahumana is one of the six Darshans (schools) of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is aetiology, the study of the causes and origins of things, and it covers history, sociology and other social sciences. Its colour is yellow. It is led by Sage Baladhuri.

Leadership: Baladhuri is the current Vahumana Sage.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Vahumana is active under Baladhuri.

123.content:
Voynich Guild (also: the Voynich Guild, Voynich): The Voynich Guild is a commerce guild of local merchants based in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, and one of the most powerful forces in the region. With no government in Nasha Town, it is the nearest thing to a regulator. It manages trade deals, imports and exports, business certificates and many disputes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Voynich Guild remains Nasha Town's leading merchant body, with Tarno speaking for it in the League.

124.content:
Wanderer's Troupe (also: Swordsman's Troupe, the Wanderer's Troupe, Wanderers' Troupe): The Wanderer's Troupe, also called the Swordsman's Troupe, was a group of travelling musicians who were also skilled fighters. A thousand years ago they wandered across Teyvat, then ended their journey in Mondstadt, where they stormed the city to overthrow its tyrannical aristocracy. They failed, and the troupe broke up, but its memory lives on in artifact and weapon lore and in the people it inspired.

Status as of 7.1: The troupe is long gone. Nothing in canon through 7.1 shows its members returning, though the Wanderer's Troupe weapons and artifacts survive in the world.

125.content:
Wangsheng Funeral Parlor (also: Wangsheng, Wangsheng Parlor, Hall of Rebirth, Wangsheng-tang): The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is the funeral house of Liyue Harbor, on Feiyun Slope. It arranges burials, cremations and memorial rites for the dead of every rank, and it also performs the rites that send off adepti. It is run by the Hu family, which has held the Directorship for 77 generations. The current Director is Hu Tao, and Zhongli works there as consultant. The parlour also keeps a duty most people never see: watching the border between life and death, and burning away the fetor that leaks across it.

Leadership: Hu Tao is the 77th Director. She is a cheerful, eccentric young woman who treats the work seriously beneath the jokes. Zhongli is the parlour's consultant; Hu Tao teases him for being old-fashioned while trusting him more than anyone else.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the parlour is active. Hu Tao is Director and Zhongli remains consultant. Hu Tao appears in the 6.3 (Luna IV) Lantern Rite story with her friends, but no story about the parlour itself was found for 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

126.content:
Watatsumi Army (also: Watatsumi Troops, the Resistance, Sangonomiya Rebels, Sangonomiya troops, Sangonomiya Samurai, Watatsumi forces): The Watatsumi Army, also called the Resistance, is the armed force of Watatsumi Island in Inazuma. It was raised against the Vision Hunt Decree and the Shogunate's Sakoku order and is led by Sangonomiya Kokomi, the island's Divine Priestess, with General Gorou commanding in the field. Its soldiers are called Sangonomiya samurai or troops, and the Shogunate calls them rebels. The decree is now abolished, so the army works as peacekeepers and rebuilders.

Leadership: Sangonomiya Kokomi, the Divine Priestess, is the supreme leader. She is a brilliant strategist who plans for every scenario in advance. General Gorou, who is open-hearted and trusted by his troops, leads the soldiers on the battlefield.

Status as of 7.1: The Vision Hunt Decree has been repealed and the Watatsumi Army no longer fights the Shogunate. It serves as peacekeepers and helps the island recover, while still clearing out Fatui remnants.

127.content:
Yae Publishing House (also: Yae-dou): Yae Publishing House is a light-novel publisher and bookshop in Inazuma City. Yae Miko, the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, founded it and is its editor-in-chief. She started it, by her own account, because she wanted more entertaining light novels to read. Its flagship event is the periodic "This Novel Is Amazing!" writing contest, and its books are read well beyond Inazuma.

Leadership: Yae Miko decides what gets published. She is known to be warm and bookish in the house and openly mercenary about profit, and she teases her authors about their deadline excuses.

Reputation: Inazuma's publishing giant: famed for light novels, bestsellers and the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest. Fans make pilgrimages to buy its books.

Status as of 7.1: Active and thriving as of Version 7.1. Miko still runs it, the bookshop in Inazuma City still sells its books, and the contest is still held.

128.content:
Yaksha (also: Yakshas, the Yakshas, Five Yakshas, Five Mighty Yakshas, Guardian Yakshas, Vigilant Yaksha, yaksha adepti): The yakshas were a fierce kind of illuminated beast-adepti. After the Archon War, Morax summoned them to wage an unending war on the monsters, plagues and curses born from the hatred of defeated gods. Five were the strongest and became known as the Five Yakshas. The work burdened them with karmic debt, and nearly all died, went mad or vanished. Only Alatus, now called Xiao, remains.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Xiao is the only living yaksha. The 5.x to 7.1 material checked adds nothing new about the yakshas.

129.content:
Yashiro Commission (also: Yashiro Bugyo, Yashiro Bugyou, Sha-bugyou, Yashiro Commissioner): The Yashiro Commission (Sha-bugyou, "Commission of Shrines") is one of the three bodies of Inazuma's Tri-Commission, alongside the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions. It handles shrines, festivals, ceremonies and the cultural life of the people, and is run by the Kamisato Clan from the Kamisato Estate on Narukami Island. The Commissioner is Kamisato Ayato. His sister Ayaka is its warm public face. Behind the festivals it also commands the secret Shuumatsuban ninja.

Leadership: Kamisato Ayato is the Yashiro Commissioner and head of the Kamisato Clan. He keeps a low public profile, works on government affairs and is known as clever, polite and hard to read. His sister Kamisato Ayaka, the Shirasagi Himegimi ("White Heron Princess"), is the clan's popular public face.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Yashiro Commission is active under Ayato and remains based at the Kamisato Estate.

130.content: Yinyuan Hall (also: Yinyuan Chamber): Yinyuan Hall governs Liyue's salt industry and is one of the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing. Its members descend from people who survived the fall of Sal Terrae, the last haven of the God of Salt, Havria. The Hall tells a story of her death that the truth contradicts.

131.content:
Yun-Han Opera Troupe (also: Yun-Han Troupe, Yunhan Opera Troupe, Yun-Han Opera Company): The Yun-Han Opera Troupe is the best-known Liyue Opera company in Liyue Harbor. The house of Yun has run it for generations, and its current director is the opera singer and playwright Yun Jin. It performs regularly at Heyu Tea House.

Leadership: Yun Jin is the director, the troupe's lead performer and the author of its new plays. Her manager Yunning handles bookings and press.

History: The Yun family were famous weaponsmiths about 500 years ago, and over time the family took up Liyue Opera. By the time of Yun Jin's grandfather the Yun-Han Opera Troupe existed.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. Yun Jin still directs the troupe and performs in Liyue Harbor.
